notes.rootFontSize: 16px; rem utilities resolve at standard values. The body defaults to 14px. Type scale in explicit px: 2xs 11/16 and 2xl 24/32 are configured but unused.
notes.themes: Light on :root; dark under prefers-color-scheme: dark. colorMeta.<token>.dark is the dark value. Tokens are HSL channel variables consumed as hsl(var(--token)).

narrative.overview:
sThree Browser is the category-standard storage console, built to the polish bar of Linear, Vercel, GitHub and the R2/S3 consoles. Grey-white surfaces, near-black ink, soft hairlines and rounded, inset rows. One blue marks what you can do next and what you have selected. Nothing glows, nothing floats unless it actually sits above the page, and motion is limited to state feedback. It deliberately rejects the dark glassmorphic shadcn look and its habit of animating everything.

The interface is made for repeat work, comfortable rather than cramped. A 16px root with a 14px body and 36px controls reads at a normal desktop size while a long listing still fits on one screen. Figures use tabular alignment so sizes and dates line up in columns. Security state is part of the chrome: the vault status card with its auto-lock countdown sits at the top of the sidebar on every screen. The full light and dark themes follow the system setting (`prefers-color-scheme`), and there is no in-app theme toggle.
keyCharacteristics: Neutral surfaces in three tones (white content, blue-grey sidebar, near-white subtle bands) separated by soft 1px hairlines.
One blue accent, used only for primary action, selection and focus.
System UI type stack, px ramp from 12.5px to 20px with a 14px body, tabular figures for every number.
Monospace only for literal strings the user types or copies verbatim.
Rows are inset rounded fills, not ruled lines.
Flat at rest, with hairline-scale shadows on controls and cards; real shadows reserved for floating layers.
Light and dark themes from the same HSL channel tokens.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: Blue appears only for primary actions, selection and focus. It is never decoration, never a link colour in running text, never an icon tint for folders or file types. A file icon turns Selection Ink only while its row is selected.

rules.name: The Meaningful State Rule
rules.body: Green, amber and red appear only where they carry a state the user must read. Folder and file icons are neutral (`fg-muted`, folders with a 15% fill of the same colour). User-chosen group colours appear only as the 8px dot beside the group name.

rules.name: The Raised Selection Exception
rules.body: The active sidebar connection is the one selection that is not a blue wash: it is a raised canvas pill (card shadow plus a 1px hairline ring) in ink at 500 weight, and its database icon in Selection Ink carries the selection. On the grey sidebar a white pill reads as "this one is open" without a second blue surface competing with the table selection.

rules.name: The px Ramp Rule
rules.body: The root font size is 16px, so rem utilities resolve at their standard values (a 0.25rem step is 4px; `h-9` is 36px). The body defaults to 14px. The type scale is declared in explicit px with paired line heights (12.5/18, 14/21, 15/22, 17/26, 20/28). Touch-critical sizes stay explicit px: mobile list rows are exactly 44px.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every number (sizes, dates, counts, percentages, countdowns, ETags) uses tabular figures in the sans face. Metadata is never set in monospace to make it align.

rules.name: The Literal String Rule
rules.body: Monospace marks strings that must be read or typed exactly: object keys and prefixes (the key block, the drop-target path, the new-folder prefix), the folder name typed to confirm a folder deletion, secret and credential fields (password inputs, access keys, masked key previews), the connection identity fields (bucket, region, endpoint inputs), share URLs, and code or file content (the CORS rule, text previews, raw error detail). Every other field, including displayed size, type, date, storage class and ETag, is sans.

rules.name: The Phantom Column Rule
rules.body: The table is `table-fixed` and uses full-width `colSpan` rows (the parent-folder row). The Modified column therefore renders only at 640px and up through a JS media hook. Never hide a column in this table with CSS alone; it leaves a phantom column.

rules.name: The Search Threshold Rule
rules.body: The sidebar connection search appears only when there are more than 6 connections. Below that the list fits without scrolling and the field is noise.

rules.name: The Shadow-on-Float Rule
rules.body: Only layers that actually sit above the page (tray, toasts, dialogs, drawer) get a real shadow (popover or dialog). Resting elements carry at most the hairline-scale `xs` or `card` lift. Panels, tables and the sidebar are never lifted.

rules.name: The Persistent Failure Rule
rules.body: Completed uploads can be dismissed. Failed uploads stay, washed red with the reason in red text, until the user dismisses them. Toasts for other notices appear bottom-right.

dos: **Do** keep blue to primary action, selection and focus (the One Blue Rule); the only non-wash selection is the raised active connection pill.
**Do** set every number in tabular sans figures, and monospace only for literal strings (the Literal String Rule).
**Do** write touch-critical and column sizes in explicit px (44px mobile rows, 272px sidebar, 360px panel).
**Do** render conditional table columns in JS when the table is `table-fixed` with `colSpan` rows.
**Do** draw row hover and selection as inset 10px-rounded fills, not as divider lines.
**Do** make bulk destructive actions show their scope, require typing the target's name, and report progress and errors inside the dialog.
**Do** keep vault state visible on every unlocked screen.
**Do** keep motion to state feedback: 100–150ms fills, a 0.98 press, 200ms for dialogs, the drawer and progress, and nothing under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
donts: **Don't** colour folder or file-type icons; they stay in muted ink.
**Don't** use green, amber or red for anything that is not a state.
**Don't** lift resting surfaces beyond the `xs` or `card` shadow; only floating layers get the popover or dialog shadow.
**Don't** add uppercase, letter-spaced labels above headings; section labels are 12.5px sentence case.
**Don't** bring back the dark glassmorphic look: no translucent blurred panels or cards and no glows. Translucency is limited to the sticky table header and the 2px dialog-scrim blur.
